biological.citation: Non-Synaptic Function and Localization of Syntaxin-Binding Protein 1 in a Mouse Model of STXBP1-Related Epileptic Encephalopathy (PMID: 41510908)
biological.summary: STXBP1 is expressed in both synaptic and cytosolic fractions of the brain, interacting with neuronal cytoskeleton and membrane periodic structures including alpha II Spectrin and ARPC2. Sparse Stxbp1 knockout in mouse forebrain caused cell-autonomous neuronal death, and pathogenic mutants rescued cell survival but impaired dendritic growth. These findings indicate STXBP1 has diverse non-synaptic functions, including regulation of membrane cytoskeleton protein trafficking.

biological.citation: Impaired neuronal activity and differential gene expression in STXBP1 encephalopathy patient iPSC-derived GABAergic neurons (PMID: 33961044)
biological.summary: Patient-derived iPSC GABAergic neurons with STXBP1 pathogenic variants showed only ~20% reduction in STXBP1 protein despite 50% reduction in mRNA, and exhibited dysfunctional maturation with reduced spontaneous spikes and bursts by microelectrode array. Gene expression analysis revealed dysregulation of epilepsy-, neurodevelopment-, and neurodegeneration-associated genes (KCNH1, KCNH5, CNN3, RASGRF1, SEMA3A, SIAH3, INPP5F), supporting GABAergic dysfunction as a key contributor to STXBP1 encephalopathy pathogenesis.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - α-Synuclein pathology in Drosophila melanogaster is exacerbated by haploinsufficiency of Rop: Connecting STXBP1 encephalopathy with α-synucleinopathies (ASHG 2023)
biological.summary: Haploinsufficiency of Rop, the Drosophila STXBP1 homolog, significantly increased insoluble α-synuclein aggregates, reduced dopamine neuron numbers, and impaired adult locomotor function in α-synuclein-transgenic flies. Trehalose feeding reduced insoluble α-synuclein and restored locomotion, providing the first in vivo model evidence that STXBP1 acts as a molecular chaperone suppressing α-synuclein aggregation.

biological.citation: ASHG 2019 - PgmNr 3136: Humanized STXBP1 animal models as a precision medicine approach to detecting pathogenicity in clinical variants (ASHG 2019)
biological.summary: Human STXBP1 coding sequence was inserted as a gene replacement of unc-18 in C. elegans, rescuing locomotion and electrophysiology defects of unc-18 knockouts. Known pathogenic variants (R292H, R406H, R388X) installed into the humanized locus showed quantifiable functional defects in chemotaxis and electrophysiology assays, with R388X displaying a dominant-negative phenotype approximately 3-fold more severe than heterozygous full gene knockout.

biological.citation: CASK, APBA1, and STXBP1 collaborate during insulin secretion (PMID: 33159991)
biological.summary: Co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry demonstrated that CASK, APBA1, and STXBP1 form a tripartite complex during insulin secretion in pancreatic cells. CASK enhanced APBA1-STXBP1 interaction and mediated their trafficking from cytoplasm to plasma membrane; high fatty acid stimulation reduced expression of all three proteins and impaired insulin secretion, while CASK overexpression rescued this defect.

biological.citation: Impaired cortico-striatal excitatory transmission triggers epilepsy (PMID: 31015467)
biological.summary: Stxbp1 haplodeficient mice exhibited absence seizures with spike-and-wave discharges initiated by reduced excitatory transmission from the neocortex to striatal fast-spiking interneurons (FSIs). Selective Stxbp1 deficiency in cortico-striatal but not cortico-thalamic neurons reproduced seizures, and pharmacological AMPA receptor potentiation in the striatum suppressed spike-and-wave discharges, identifying impaired cortico-striatal excitatory transmission as a key epileptogenic circuit mechanism.

biological.citation: STXBP1 encephalopathy: Connecting neurodevelopmental disorders with α-synucleinopathies? (PMID: 31221716)
biological.summary: STXBP1 (Munc18-1) controls SNARE complex formation and synaptic vesicle exocytosis, and genetic knockout leads to widespread perinatal neurodegeneration. Recent evidence indicates STXBP1 also controls the self-replicating aggregation of α-synuclein, linking STXBP1 function to synucleinopathies including Parkinson disease. This review proposes that concurrent synucleinopathic mechanisms may further impair neural development in STXBP1 encephalopathy.

biological.citation: Homozygous STXBP1 variant causes encephalopathy and gain-of-function in synaptic transmission (PMID: 31855252)
biological.summary: In Munc18-1 null mouse neurons, the homozygous disease variant L446F caused a 2-fold increase in evoked synaptic transmission with reduced paired-pulse plasticity, representing a gain-of-function in release probability distinct from the loss-of-function seen with heterozygous mutations. Protein stability of L446F was less dramatically affected than previously reported heterozygous mutants, demonstrating that STXBP1 mutations can produce divergent cellular effects while sharing an encephalopathic phenotype.

biological.citation: HSV-1 latency-associated transcript miR-H3 and miR-H4 target STXBP1 and GABBR2 genes (PMID: 37668872)
biological.summary: HSV-1 LAT-encoded miRNAs miR-H3 and miR-H4 were shown by bioinformatic prediction and luciferase assay to target the 3'UTR of STXBP1, reducing its expression. Overexpression of miR-H4, miR-H3, or the full LAT transcript in HEK293T cells decreased STXBP1 mRNA by 0.059-, 0.237-, and 0.84-fold respectively, identifying STXBP1 as a component of the GABAergic pathway targeted during HSV-1 latency.

biological.citation: PQBP1-dependent alternative RNA splicing underlies high calorie diet-induced cognitive impairment (PMID: 40502014)
biological.summary: Network analysis of high-fat diet-induced alternative splicing changes identified CASK and Cacnb1 as core molecules that regulate STXBP1, a causative gene for infantile epilepsy syndrome and essential factor for synaptic vesicle release, through direct protein interaction. HFD-induced alternative splicing isoforms of CASK and Cacnb1 impaired presynaptic vesicle release in primary neurons, and AAV-mediated rescue of these genes restored synaptic and cognitive function in HFD mice.
